note: Same approach as the North Ridge; placing the moraine bivy on this line is a reasonable inference, not confirmed.
Route has no documented approach; assumed to share the north route's Middle Fork ford from the horse camp.
'Hardscrabble Horse Camp' and 'Williams Lake' are duplicates of the longer-named entries; the exact Iron Cap line from the Middle Fork is thinly documented.
Barely documented tower; assumed to use the same Lemah Meadow approach and camps as the rest of the Lemah massif.
Lemah Meadows basin camp is the higher climbers' bivy under the east face; which of the two is more used is unclear.
Unsure whether the route leaves the Waptus trail before or after Waptus Lake; placed as on the way.
Entire list is Heliotrope Ridge and Easton camps; this route approaches over Ptarmigan Ridge, so the Portals camp and Camp Kiser are added. Unsure how often parties descend Coleman-Deming instead.
Cougar Divide is this route's own ridge; Deadhorse basin sits below the way onto Chowder Ridge. Unsure how close the basin is to the Cougar line.

Parties leave the North Fork trail before Grizzly Creek and bivy on a bench below the technical climbing; that bench is added. The Goode Glacier camps serve the Northeast Buttress. Unsure exactly where Walker Park sits relative to the turn-off.
Lateral moraine waypoint looks like the same ground as the glacier toe entry; the approach text and the camp entries describe slightly different lines, so unsure which camp most use.
Rarely climbed; Kool-Aid Lake and the Spider-Formidable Col are the likely bases but the exact approach to the Formidable Glacier face is uncertain.
Uncertain which side parties reach the west-face pocket glacier from; Kool-Aid Lake assumed, Pelton Basin possible.
Assumes a Brush Creek side approach from Graybeal; no detailed route description for this peak was found.

Least certain of the batch: no clear record of Dana's standard camp; the upper Elwha / Bailey Range bivies and Chicago Camp are the reasonable bases; Dodger Point might serve a ridge approach but is unconfirmed; Mary's Falls Camp dropped as a duplicate of the Lillian/Mary's entry.
No approach text; Low Divide is the base for all three Seattle routes; could not confirm which side Noyes Basin is entered from, so Elwha trail camps are kept onRoute tentatively.
Assumed to share the Colchuck Glacier approach from the south end of the lake; less certain than the glacier routes.
Witches Tower is reached from the top of Aasgard Pass; camp at Colchuck Lake or go car-to-car. Low confidence on how often it is split.
Normally climbed in a link-up from the Chiwawa basin side; the added bench is inferred from the East Ridge approach, not confirmed for this line.
Parties camp in the basin below Pass No Pass or at Buck Creek Pass; both added. Elevation of the Pass No Pass basin camp not confirmed, so omitted.
Route-specific basin camp first; the Emerald-Saska basin is also commonly used for Cardinal. Unsure the two basins are distinct places.

A day scramble from the Foss River road with no camp on the north ridge; the car campground is the staging camp. Unsure whether the Bald Eagle Lake cirque lies on the north-ridge line, so it was dropped.
Cedar Creek side camps; unsure whether the meadow camps above the falls lie before the route leaves the trail.
Cool/Gerdine Basin Camp has no notes; assumed to be a spot in the basin traverse between White Pass and Glacier Gap.
Parties base at Buck Creek Pass or the High Pass camps; the route also lists a Little Giant approach whose exact camp is unclear, so the Napeequa camps were dropped.

Low confidence: the Green Mountain approach has first-night camps near Horse Lake saddle (added), but where parties base for the north-side route (Kindy head vs a basin west of Misch) is thinly documented.
Normally a long day from the road; unsure whether the East Peak line via Green Ridge Lake is part of this multi-summit route, so that lake was dropped.
Hester Lake is the documented overnight for Price; the Dingford roadside pull-outs are kept as the trailhead option but current dispersed-camping rules there are unclear.
Done in a big day or with a bivy at the base with running water; bivy elevation not confirmed so omitted.
Traverse Merritt-Mastiff-Howard-Rock; Crescent Lake is the midpoint camp, Rock Lake assumed on the descent via the Rock Mountain trail.
Day route via Maynard Burn and Baldy; Cedar Lake is reached from the Gray Wolf River, a different approach, so it is dropped. Unsure whether parties camp on the ridge crest.
Unsure: this route is described from Obstruction Point over Cameron Pass, while the long-standing base for Claywood is Dose Meadows on the Dosewallips side; both kept as main.
Unsure: starts from the Nooksack Cirque trailhead, and the Hannegan campground is kept only as the nearby car camp.
Low confidence: south route base taken from the route's own waypoints; the Whatcom Pass and Perfect Pass waypoints duplicate the listed camps.
Luna Creek approach from Luna Camp into the cirque; the cirque floor camp is assumed as the base for the east-face glacier.
Wild Lake added as base without elevation; Terror Basin kept for the southern corridor; low confidence on corridor camps.
Swiss is done only as part of crest traverses; Luna Col base assumed from the Big Beaver approach text; low confidence.
Sixteen Mile base; route text also mentions Low Divide and the Skyline trail, so the exact line is uncertain; the Elip Creek group entry duplicates listed camps.
Upper Cathedral Lake is standard; unsure whether the West Route actually passes through the Amphitheater upper basin, kept as onRoute.
Unsure whether the 6,600 ft basin waypoint is a separate spot above the lake or the same camp.
Added the Beauty Creek tarn as main; unsure whether the Robinson Creek valley entry already means this tarn.
Uncertain: this is mostly a day hike and no listed camp is on the Windy Creek trail, so the added plateau camp is a best guess.

South-face rock route on Dome from the western approach; camp at Itswoot Ridge or the Dome Glacier high bivies is inferred from the standard Dome approach, not confirmed for this rarely repeated line.

Approach text is empty; assumed the north-end Ptarmigan Traverse approach from Cascade Pass, with Yang Yang Lakes the natural base and White Rock Lakes the option for traverse parties already past the Le Conte Glacier.
Stored approach is the Upper Dungeness trail, so Home Lake is the base with Boulder Shelter on the way; not confirmed for this rarely climbed buttress.
Fisher Camp kept on the assumption that the traverse exits down Fisher Creek; the exit varies.
The camp for this route is Crater Lake, which was missing; Devils Park is on the Jackita Ridge trail beyond the junction. Crater Lake elevation not confirmed, so omitted.
Sparse record; assumed to share the Nohokomeen approach from May Creek, so it gets the same camps.

A party record camps at the 6,000 ft basin WNW of point 7001 after passing Jerry Lakes; order of the two mains is a judgment call, and whether these camps are in Ross Lake NRA or the Pasayten Wilderness is not confirmed.
Added the Little Jack knoll camp; water there and which side of the boundary it sits on are not confirmed, and fast parties do the route car-to-car.
Parties camp at the old cabin or at Libby Lake just above; the cabin camp was missing. Its water source is assumed, not confirmed.
Added Crater Lakes as the camp for this approach; elevation not confirmed, and the route is often done in a day.
Cooney Lake is the standard base; Upper Eagle Lake is only on the way for parties doing the Eagle Lakes loop, a judgment call.
No bivy record found for the arete; assumed to use the shared White Salmon approach ridge and bivy, which is uncertain.
Parties bivy on the slabs or saddle above Price Lake below the glacier; descent route varies, so the Fisher Chimneys camps as on-route is a judgment call.
Added the lower White Salmon bivy, which was missing; elevation omitted as not confirmed.
Couloir Camp is the last flat ground before the technical face; Barclay Lake is the valley base below the face, but the exact approach link from the lake is uncertain.
North-side couloir with little published approach beta; assumed to be reached from Crescent Creek Basin over a crest col, which is uncertain.
New-route line with no published camp; Crescent Creek Basin is assumed as for the other Crescent Creek Spires.
The Blob sits north of the Himmelhorn, so the Crescent Creek Basin camp and high crest bivouacs are assumed; exact camp not confirmed.
Terror Basin via the Terror Glacier is the usual base for the south side; some parties reach the Pyramid from Crescent Creek Basin instead, so this is a judgement call.
Flapjack Lakes is the standard base for Needle Pass and the South Corner; Black and White Lakes kept as the overflow camp, a judgment call.
Lake Sundown is the usual base; unsure exactly where the Belview/Six Ridge camps fall relative to the Olson way, kept as on-route since they are on the same ridge trail.
The Lichtenhorn stands over Lake Valhalla, the natural camp; unsure this rarely climbed line is ever done overnight.
Rarely climbed; the Tye-Spinnaker basin is mainly a winter camp and summer parties likely do it in a day. Waypoint basin entry dropped as a duplicate. Unsure whether the basin is inside a wilderness.
Added Thunder Mountain Lakes as the closest camp to the north face (elevation not confirmed, left out); Trap Lake kept as the common camp.
West Face Wall is reached over Stuart Pass; parties bivy in the boulder basin near 6,000 ft below the wall or at Headlight Basin, otherwise car-to-car; descent camp use unclear.
Beverly Turnpike to Ingalls Creek and up the south side; the 6,000 ft basin waypoint is assumed to be on this route's gully, not verified.
North side from the Stuart Lake trailhead via the eastern fork; often a long day; unsure whether the Mountaineer Creek bench sits on this line, so dropped.
North approach from Stuart Lake trailhead; exact relation of the 6,800 ft lower basin waypoint to the north basin bivies is uncertain.
North side approach via the climbers' path off the Stuart Lake trail; bench assumed as base, often done in a day.
Same Blue Lake Trailhead approach as the group's other faces; this route is rarely repeated so its overnight use is unclear.

Shares the Silver Star Glacier route's Burgundy Col approach up to the glacier before trending toward the northeast side; the two Silver Star Creek camps serve the unrelated east-side approach and were dropped. Thinly documented route, so confidence in the exact camp used near the top is lower.
